reasoning: Xi Jinping has eliminated term limits, controls the military and party apparatus, and faces no visible internal threat. Removal would require an extraordinary event like a coup or incapacitating health crisis, both extremely unlikely within 18 months. The market's 7% implied probability significantly overstates the risk.
evidence_points: Xi removed presidential term limits in 2018, signaling indefinite rule and institutional lock on power.
Anti-corruption campaigns and personnel reshuffles have reinforced his control over the party and security forces.
Historical precedent shows CCP leaders are rarely removed involuntarily outside of death or severe scandal; no credible opposition exists.
sources_consulted: Consensus of credible reporting on CCP internal dynamics
Analysis of Xi's consolidation of power post-2018
Historical data on Chinese leadership transitions
